method: Historical reconstruction of a first-write release anchor with a non-zero SBOM hash. Gas units come from the v1.0.1 revision-1 mainnet receipts and are priced from the retained daily base-fee statistics. Arbitrum aggregate costs are proportionally rebased to the final 100,095 gas units. OP Mainnet uses 99,512 gas with the observed 1,000,000 wei priority fee and 2,257,258,350 wei l1Fee. Figures are counterfactual: what a release anchor would have cost had it been submitted at that moment, not a fee that was paid. The v1.0.1 revision-1 receipts validate the fee arithmetic using their own gasUsed.

collection.transport: JSON-RPC eth_getBlockByNumber and eth_getTransactionReceipt, issued from the browser because the analysis sandbox cannot reach these endpoints
collection.completeness: 365/365 samples on every network, no gaps

arbitrumOne.feeModel: Nitro prices the L1 posting cost as extra gas units inside gasUsed. The v1.0.1 revision-1 receipt validates the multiplication. Historical release pricing holds its 100,095-gas shape fixed, so it understates cost when L1 posting is expensive. Figures below are therefore a floor at the tail, not a point estimate.
arbitrumOne.senderTip: none observed; effectiveGasPrice equalled the block base fee exactly
arbitrumOne.note: The monthly medians show a floor change, not congestion: the network's minimum base fee moved from 0.01 to 0.02 gwei around January 2026. Congestion appears in the tail, not the median.

opMainnet.feeModel: OP Stack splits the fee. gasUsed x effectiveGasPrice covers L2 execution, and a separate l1Fee on the receipt covers posting to L1. The recorded fee in mainnet.md omits l1Fee because ethers' receipt.fee does not include it.
opMainnet.senderTip: Historical reconstruction holds the v1.0.1 revision-1 priority fee fixed at 1,000,000 wei (0.001 gwei), derived from the 1,000,366 wei effective gas price minus the 366 wei block base fee.
opMainnet.reconstructionBasis: units x (base fee + observed 1,000,000 wei tip) + observed l1Fee of 2.257258350e9 wei
opMainnet.note: The priority fee and l1Fee are held at their v1.0.1 revision-1 values. Variation comes only from the retained base-fee aggregates, so historical changes in either fixed input are not reflected.

zkSyncEra.feeModel: EraVM prices execution and published data together through its own gas model. Units are not comparable with the EVM chains.
zkSyncEra.senderTip: none; effectiveGasPrice equalled the block base fee
zkSyncEra.note: The base fee was identical in all 365 samples across the year, at 0.04525 gwei. zkSync Era holds its L2 gas price at a floor rather than letting it float with demand, so the anchor cost has no observed distribution at daily resolution. This is a property of the network's pricing policy, not a measurement artefact.

ethereum.role: L1 context for the rollups' posting costs
ethereum.blobBaseFee: not reported; the derivation from excessBlobGas produced implausible values, most likely because the update fraction changed in a fork after the version implemented. Left out rather than published wrong.

phaseAValidation.note: The receipt's 1,000,000 wei priority fee and 2,257,258,350 wei l1Fee are the fixed values used by the historical reconstruction.

limitations: Daily resolution can miss intraday peaks. A dense pass over the worst days would tighten the tail: npm run fees:history -- --days 30 --interval 2 --out fee-history-dense.json
Arbitrum release-anchor figures hold gas units fixed, so they understate the tail, where L1 posting can consume more units than in the priced v1.0.1 transaction shape.
OP holds the observed 1,000,000 wei priority fee and l1Fee fixed rather than reconstructing either across time.
The original per-sample raw series is not archived. A pinned collection rerun reconstructs a compatible series but cannot prove the exact original block identifiers.
USD figures use a single approximate rate of $1900/ETH and are illustrative only.
